blocking_findings.why: Fixture line 2 is `name: checking:accessibility`; the checklist's A17 states verbatim that Claude Code does not load a colon name at all from v2.1.218 with only a debug-log trace. The Manifests scenario (subagent silently absent from the roster after an upgrade) is exactly what the criterion documents. Deterministic, High is the only defensible rank.

Lines 11-13 enumerate report fields and bound nothing; A7's guarantee is that the return preserves the context saving that justifies delegation. The Manifests scenario (40 routes x site-wide failure returning more tokens than an inline run) actually bites.

Axe genuinely does not emit a codebase remediation, the body grants Read only for routes.json, and 'the fix' has no observable source — a direct D2 (ground in evidence) breach. The Manifests scenario (an invented hex value the parent applies) is a realistic hallucination path.

A26 covers exactly this: a subagent reporting third-party/rendered content upward with no content-is-data rule, and the checklist notes the v2.1.210 output scan is partial. Borderline in that the 'site' may be entirely first-party, but axe output carries page text either way and the Manifests scenario (CMS-authored node text quoted into the report, with unrestricted Bash present) is defensible at Medium.

The body asks for fixes, grants Bash, and never states a report-don't-modify boundary; C8's explicit-scope guarantee plus the Opus 5 scope-expansion note the finding cites make the Manifests scenario (silent template edit reported as resolved) plausible. The C8 key mapping is slightly loose — C8's text is about breadth of application — but the defect and severity hold.

Line 13 stakes a coverage-vs-silence guarantee while the body offers no could-not-check category; D1 (permit abstention) is the right key and the Manifests scenario (9 of 12 routes scanned reads as a clean check) breaches the definition's own stated guarantee.

Three operations named with zero specification in a definition that cannot ask (A9), for a verification role where run-to-run comparability matters; the Manifests scenario (harness change read as a regression) bites. Borderline toward inflated — the finding itself concedes a repo script may fix it in practice — but it is honestly marked low-confidence/inferential and the fixture workspace ships nothing that pins the commands, so Medium is defensible.

grader_summary: The run nailed the scenario's target: a High A17 finding stating the colon name prevents loading entirely from v2.1.218, that the only trace is the debug log, with a concrete Manifests scenario, ranked first, and the filename explicitly cleared as a non-defect — matching expected_output exactly. All nine evidence quotes verify verbatim against the fixture; every cited criterion key resolves in the two criteria files; the verdict arithmetic (1 High + 6 Medium = 'not yet — 7 blocking') is correct. The six additional Mediums are all genuine or defensibly so, with Findings 5 (loose C8 key mapping) and 7 (low-confidence, self-disclosed) the closest calls — a mild severity-generosity tendency worth watching across the campaign, but nothing inflated enough to reclassify.
